resolved_by: The 2016 amendment to Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(4)(A), with its Advisory Committee Note, addressed the circuit split and adopted the rule that forfeiting a timeliness objection does not make an untimely post-judgment motion timely.
issue: Does a party's failure to object in the district court to the untimeliness of a post-judgment motion make that motion 'timely' for purposes of tolling the appeal deadline under Appellate Rule 4(a)(4)(A)?

sides.position: A forfeited objection to the untimeliness of a Rule 59(e) motion makes the motion timely for purposes of Appellate Rule 4(a)(4)(A).
cases: Nat'l Ecological Found. v. Alexander, 496 F.3d 466 (6th Cir. 2007)

sides.position: Forfeiture of a timeliness objection in the district court does not render an untimely motion timely for purposes of Appellate Rule 4(a)(4)(A).
cases: Lizardo v. United States, 619 F.3d 273 (3d Cir. 2010)

this_court: Adopts the view that forfeiture of a timeliness objection does not make an untimely motion timely, relying on the 2016 Advisory Committee Note and aligning with the Third Circuit.
quote: The 2016 amendment to Appellate Rule 4(a)(4)(A) addressed a circuit split about whether a post-judgment motion is “timely” for the purposes of tolling where the district court extended the post-judgment motion deadline and no party objected to the extension.
